newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pechiney sees second half loss.
newsitem.headline: Pechiney sees second half loss.

text.p: Aluminium group Pechniney said it expected to post a net loss for the second half of 1996 against a pro-forma 1995 second half profit of about one hundred million francs.
It said the loss forecast was due to a fall in the price of aluminium.
Pechiney said that the fall of aluminium on the London Metals Exchange had led the company to stop some production lines for drink cans and the closure of a plant in the U.S.
It said the situation also had repercussions for its Rhenalu activities.

"Taking account of these elements, and more generally the absence of any signs of a real recovery in Europe, the group believes that the last quarter of the year will see a significant deterioration in sales and results," Pechiney said.
"In these conditions, the net result for the second half, which was a profit of about hundred million francs in 1995 (on a prof-forma basis) will be a loss," it said.

It added that the 1996 results would also be affected by exceptional provisions for its Challenge restructuring plan and for a legal case, still underway, about breach of patent by American National Can.
